bet.text: Make the whole path of the note as seamless as possible, starting with an intake across the full width of the robot.

demand.text: Short cycles: drivers can run into a note and pick it up instead of spending time on it. The team says it thinks about high-level play and strategies at the start of the season, when it designs the robot. It shoots from the wing line.

auto.text: A commenter says its auto consistently won two center notes in division eliminations and on Einstein.

cycle.text: Drive into a note; side rollers funnel it to the center, a ramp leads it to the feeder rollers, and the cannon shoots. For the amp, the shooter comes down and the note follows its path and shoots back out.
Championship playoff commenters saw it mainly passing to 254, and one saw a move to cycling in Finals 2.

endgame.text: Unspooling the winch lets the hanger arms come up; at a certain height the hanger forks come out. The driver lines up and starts the hanging sequence, which winches the arms down on the chain.
Commenters credit it with a consistent trap.

fallback.text: A reply that reads as 254's says 1323 could change roles, for example stealing notes in the opponent's front court and passing them, or cover for losing a robot early.

gave_up.text: The team had to use a rectangular drivetrain, and says the under-bumper intake compensates.
After the Einstein finals commenters said its large size made it easier to defend, and one that its high bumpers let 321 get underneath; another later said it was not that bad under defense.

changed.text: A reply that reads as 254's says the alliance changed its strategy one match too late in the Einstein finals. It had put an earlier close match against Daly down to other factors, such as 1323 running a dead battery, instead of 321's defense.

outcome.text: 45-7-1 in official play; won the Newton division; championship finalist; pick 1 of the Newton alliance on Einstein; ranked 2 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 59.80, Newton).

solves.text: Pick up a note by driving into it, with short cycle times

facts.text: Spans the entire width of the robot
Side funneling rollers, on a different gearbox, move the note toward the center

solves.text: Draw the note in without stretching or compressing it before the shot

facts.text: A 3D printed ramp and a polycarbonate sheet direct the note into the feeder rollers
A removable protective cover prevents notes from getting stuck
Very similar to the system used the year before

functions.name: Cannon
functions.type: pivoting shooter with two roller sets

solves.text: Shoot consistently from as far as the wing line, with a stable note

facts.text: Low pivot toward the back of the robot, which the team says lets it shoot from farther away
One gearbox and a transfer tube turn both sides, with a custom machined gear
One motor per side lets the two sides run at different speeds
Comes down for the amp, and the note follows its path and shoots back out

solves.text: Climb the chain with a sequence the driver starts

facts.text: Two sets of arms: hanger arms that are winched down on the chain, and hanger forks; both are on gas struts
The forks come out once the arms reach a certain height

functions.name: Drivetrain and side plates
functions.type: rectangular drivetrain with integrating side plates

solves.text: Maximize the amount of robot in the packaging

facts.text: The team says it typically uses the maximum frame perimeter and weight
The side plates tie the drivetrain and hanger together and carry the side funneling rollers

cost.text: Commenters say the size was a problem under defense; another says it was not that bad

decisions.choice: Use the maximum size and weight
decisions.because: the team wants to maximize the amount of robot in its packaging
decisions.cost: a rectangular drivetrain, which the team says the full-width intake makes up for

decisions.choice: Do not manipulate the note until it is shot
decisions.because: keeping its original shape gives consistent shots

decisions.choice: Drive both sides of the shooter pivot from one gearbox through a tube
decisions.because: there is no slippage between the sides

decisions.choice: Power each side of the shooter independently
decisions.because: different speeds keep the note's flight stable from different positions on the field
